controls.statement: Production credentials do not work in non-production environments.
controls.primary_reason: A complete approved credential inventory and fixed authentication tests can prove that each production credential is rejected by every non-production environment.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The approved secret and identity inventories enumerate every production credential and every non-production authentication boundary.
Each inventoried production credential receives a current rejected result at every non-production boundary without exposing the credential in evidence.

controls.statement: Non-production users cannot reach production control planes.
controls.primary_reason: Complete identity and production-control-plane inventories permit fixed authorization queries or denial tests for every non-production user and group.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Approved identity and control-plane inventories enumerate all non-production principals and production control-plane authorization targets.
Every inventoried non-production principal is denied access to every production control-plane target by current policy evaluation or bounded tests.

controls.statement: Non-production email, payment, notifications, and webhooks cannot accidentally contact real users.
controls.primary_reason: Approved integration and recipient inventories plus fixed sink and egress policies can prove that non-production messages cannot reach real-user destinations.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The approved environment inventory enumerates every non-production email, payment, notification, and webhook integration and every prohibited real-user destination class.
Current configuration and bounded delivery tests route every inventoried non-production integration only to approved test sinks.

controls.statement: Environment boundaries are documented and tested.
controls.primary_reason: The exact fact is the existence of current boundary documentation and successful fixed boundary tests for the approved environment inventory.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The authenticated environment record documents each approved environment boundary, identity domain, network boundary, and data boundary.
Every documented boundary has a current successful isolation test bound to the assessed configurations.

controls.statement: Production access is logged and periodically reviewed.
controls.primary_reason: A versioned review interval, production-access log, and authenticated review records make logging coverage and review freshness objectively decidable.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every production access event in the approved identity and control-plane scope produces an immutable audit event with principal, target, action, and time.
Authenticated access-review records cover all events and principals within the policy-defined review interval.

controls.statement: Configuration is version-controlled or otherwise auditable.
controls.primary_reason: Version history or an append-only audit trail can deterministically prove that every configuration revision has an immutable identity and recorded change history.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every production configuration item has an immutable version history or authenticated audit trail linking its prior and current values.

controls.statement: Configuration changes require review and approval.
controls.primary_reason: An approved change policy and authenticated workflow events can prove that no configuration change became effective without the required review and approval.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The versioned configuration policy defines required reviewer and approver roles for every configuration class.
Every effective configuration change has matching authenticated review and approval events that satisfy the bound policy.

controls.statement: Configuration has schema and type validation.
controls.primary_reason: A declared configuration schema and fixed parser can validate field types and constraints against every sealed configuration instance without interpretation.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every inventoried configuration instance validates successfully against its version-bound schema and type constraints.

controls.statement: Environment-specific values are explicit.
controls.primary_reason: A schema can require every value whose semantics vary by environment to be explicitly bound per environment rather than inherited implicitly.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every configuration field marked environment-specific in the approved schema has an explicit value or explicit not-applicable state for each environment.

controls.statement: Configuration drift is detected.
controls.primary_reason: A desired configuration snapshot and read-only observed configuration can be normalized and compared exactly to produce fixed drift results.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every inventoried environment configuration is compared with its approved desired version and all differences are reported as current drift evidence.

controls.statement: Production configuration can be reconstructed.
controls.primary_reason: A sealed reconstruction recipe can be executed in isolation and its resulting normalized configuration compared exactly with the approved production snapshot.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The approved reconstruction procedure produces a complete configuration whose normalized digest matches the production configuration digest.

controls.statement: Configuration rollback is tested.
controls.primary_reason: A version-bound rollback procedure with fixed expected state permits an isolated rollback test and exact post-rollback configuration comparison.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Current execution evidence shows the approved configuration rollback procedure restores the complete expected configuration and service state.

controls.statement: Time synchronization is monitored.
controls.primary_reason: An approved clock-skew threshold and current monitoring configuration and observations make time-synchronization monitoring objectively verifiable.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every production host or workload in the approved inventory reports clock synchronization and skew to monitoring with a current result inside the policy threshold.

controls.statement: Resource limits and timeouts are explicitly configured.
controls.primary_reason: A complete workload and client inventory can be compared with approved typed resource-limit and timeout policies without inventing universal values.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The approved policy defines required resource-limit and timeout fields, units, and ranges for each inventoried component class.
Every applicable component has explicit resource limits and timeouts that validate against its bound policy.

controls.statement: Configuration ownership and expiration dates are recorded.
controls.primary_reason: Configuration ownership identities and expiration timestamps are typed record fields whose presence, validity, scope, and freshness are objectively checkable.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every configuration item has a current accountable owner identity and an explicit expiration date or approved non-expiring classification.

controls.statement: Emergency configuration changes are captured and reviewed.
controls.primary_reason: Emergency changes can be identified from authenticated change events and checked for capture and policy-timely independent review.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every emergency configuration change is present in the authenticated change ledger with exact configuration identity, actor, values, and time.
Each emergency change has a completed review record within the policy-defined interval.

controls.statement: Every flag has an owner.
controls.primary_reason: The flag service provides a finite inventory that can be compared with an authenticated ownership record for one current owner per flag.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: A read-only query returns the complete current feature-flag inventory for the declared project scope.
Every inventoried feature flag has one current accountable owner identity in the flag record.

controls.statement: Every flag has a documented purpose.
controls.primary_reason: The requirement asks for documentation, so a nonempty purpose field bound to every inventoried flag is a fixed record-validation fact.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every inventoried feature flag has a nonempty versioned purpose field in its authenticated record.

controls.statement: Flag state is included in release and incident records.
controls.primary_reason: Flag services and release or incident record schemas expose finite state snapshots that can be compared by identity and time.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The exact feature-flag state snapshot is captured with the release identity and every incident start and material state-change time.
Each required release and incident record references the matching authenticated flag-state snapshot digest.

controls.statement: Access to change high-impact flags is restricted and audited.
controls.primary_reason: An approved high-impact flag inventory, IAM policy, and audit log permit exact authorization and logging checks for every change.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The approved policy identifies high-impact flags and the principals authorized to change each one.
Current IAM state restricts each high-impact flag to its approved principals and every change produces a complete audit event.

controls.statement: Temporary flags have removal dates.
controls.primary_reason: The flag inventory, temporary classification, and typed removal date make this a finite schema and date validation.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every feature flag classified as temporary has a valid removal date and current owner in its authenticated record.

controls.statement: Secrets are stored in an approved secret-management system.
controls.primary_reason: An approved secret-manager list and complete credential inventory can be compared to observed storage locations without judging secret quality.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The versioned policy enumerates approved secret-management systems and the complete credential scope.
Every inventoried production secret is stored only in an approved secret-management system.

controls.statement: Secrets are unique across environments.
controls.primary_reason: Privacy-preserving secret fingerprints from complete environment-specific inventories can be compared for equality without revealing secret values.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The approved secret managers return a complete scoped inventory whose keyed fingerprints show no credential value reused across environments.

controls.statement: Each workload uses its own scoped identity or credential.
controls.primary_reason: Complete workload and credential inventories permit exact one-to-one identity mapping and detection of credentials shared by multiple workloads.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The approved runtime inventory enumerates every workload and every identity or credential it uses.
Each workload maps to its own identity or credential and no scoped credential is shared outside its approved workload set.

controls.statement: Secret retrieval and use are audited.
controls.primary_reason: A complete secret-manager and workload inventory can be checked for immutable retrieval and use audit events with required fields and retention.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every secret retrieval and supported use event in the approved scope produces a current authenticated audit record with principal, secret identity, action, and time.

controls.statement: Secret rotation has been tested.
controls.primary_reason: A version-bound rotation procedure has fixed preconditions and expected old and new credential states that can be tested in isolation.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Current execution evidence shows each credential class in the approved rotation plan rotates successfully and preserves required workload access.

controls.statement: Emergency revocation has been tested.
controls.primary_reason: A version-bound revocation procedure can be exercised against test credentials with fixed denial and service-continuity expectations.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Current execution evidence shows emergency revocation invalidates the target credential and produces every policy-required continuity and audit outcome.

controls.statement: Credential expiry and rotation failures are monitored.
controls.primary_reason: An approved alert policy and current monitors can be queried for expiry and rotation-failure coverage across the complete credential inventory.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every credential class has active monitoring for expiry and rotation failures with alert thresholds and destinations matching approved policy.

controls.statement: Old credentials are invalidated after rotation.
controls.primary_reason: Rotation events identify predecessor credentials, and current authentication state can prove each predecessor is invalid after the policy transition point.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: For every completed rotation, the predecessor credential is disabled or rejected after the policy-defined transition window.

controls.statement: No default or vendor-supplied credentials remain.
controls.primary_reason: A complete deployed-product inventory and authoritative vendor default-credential catalog allow fixed comparison and rejection tests.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every deployed product with supplied credentials is matched to an authoritative catalog of its vendor default identities and values.
No cataloged default credential authenticates to the corresponding deployed product and none remains enabled in current identity state.

controls.statement: Suspected historical secret exposure has been addressed by rotation, not merely deletion from source.
controls.primary_reason: Authenticated exposure records and credential lineage make it possible to require and verify a subsequent rotation rather than accepting source deletion.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every suspected historical exposure record identifies all affected credential versions and exposure time.
Each affected credential has a later completed rotation and its exposed version is invalid in current identity state.

controls.statement: Every requirement maps to at least one verification activity.
controls.primary_reason: A complete versioned requirements inventory and authenticated verification-plan links permit an exact check that every requirement has at least one activity.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The approved release requirements record provides a complete set of stable requirement identities.
Every requirement identity is referenced by at least one current verification activity bound to the assessed release.

controls.statement: State transitions reject invalid orderings.
controls.primary_reason: A complete versioned state-machine model gives a finite transition inventory, and fixed tests can prove every prohibited ordering is rejected.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The approved state model enumerates every valid state and transition and derives the complete set of invalid orderings in scope.
Every invalid ordering in the bounded state model is rejected by current execution evidence for the assessed artifact.

controls.statement: Operations that must be idempotent are demonstrably idempotent.
controls.primary_reason: An approved idempotent-operation inventory and explicit effect model allow repeated execution and exact comparison of resulting effects.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The approved operation contract identifies every operation required to be idempotent and its observable effect identity.
Repeated execution of each inventoried operation produces exactly one approved effect under the bounded idempotency protocol.

controls.statement: Transactions are atomic where required.
controls.primary_reason: An approved transaction inventory and atomicity boundary define exact invariants that bounded fault and concurrency tests can evaluate.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The approved data contract identifies every operation requiring atomicity and the complete commit or rollback invariant for each.
Each required transaction preserves its atomicity invariant under the approved success, fault, and concurrency tests.

controls.statement: Eventually consistent operations expose correct pending and completion states.
controls.primary_reason: A versioned eventual-consistency contract can define finite pending, failed, and completed states and fixed observations for every declared operation.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The approved operation model defines pending, completion, failure, and timeout states for every eventually consistent operation.
Current tests for each inventoried operation expose only the allowed states and reach the expected terminal state within its approved bound.

controls.statement: Reconciliation detects missing, duplicated, or mismatched records.
controls.primary_reason: Injected missing, duplicate, and mismatched records with exact identities and expected findings make reconciliation detection objectively testable.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The approved reconciliation contract enumerates every record relation in scope and mechanically defines missing, duplicate, and mismatch cases for each relation.
Each reconciliation implementation detects every seeded missing, duplicated, and mismatched record in the approved fixture set without losing fixture identity.

controls.statement: Numeric precision and rounding are correct.
controls.primary_reason: Versioned numeric rules define representations, precision, and rounding boundaries, allowing exact property and boundary comparison for each calculation.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The approved calculation contract defines numeric type, precision, rounding mode, scale, and boundary behavior for every calculation in scope.
Every inventoried calculation passes exact boundary and property tests against its bound numeric contract.

controls.statement: Limits and quotas are enforced server-side.
controls.primary_reason: A complete approved limit inventory and request-surface inventory permit server-side enforcement tests that bypass every client control.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The approved policy enumerates each limit and quota, its numeric threshold, subject, reset behavior, and server endpoint scope.
Direct server requests at and beyond every limit produce the exact approved enforcement outcome independent of client behavior.

controls.statement: Scheduled jobs handle missed runs, overlapping runs, retries, and duplicate execution.
controls.primary_reason: A complete scheduled-job inventory and versioned execution contract define exact missed, overlap, retry, and duplicate scenarios with measurable state outcomes.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The approved scheduler inventory defines each job and its expected missed-run, overlap, retry, and duplicate-execution behavior.
Every inventoried job passes bounded execution tests for all four required scenario classes.

controls.statement: Background jobs preserve user, authorization, and tenant context.
controls.primary_reason: A complete background-job inventory and explicit context contract allow execution tests to compare user, authorization, and tenant identities end to end.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The approved job contract identifies required user, authorization, and tenant context fields for every background operation.
Every inventoried job preserves the exact required context values through enqueue, execution, retry, and completion tests.

controls.statement: Administrative actions produce the intended effect and audit trail.
controls.primary_reason: Versioned administrative action contracts define intended state changes and required audit fields, permitting exact execution and log comparison.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The approved administrative-action catalog defines the expected state transition and audit-event fields for every action.
Each action produces its declared state transition and matching authenticated audit event under current execution tests.

controls.statement: Test failures cannot be dismissed without evidence.
controls.primary_reason: A versioned test-gate policy and authenticated disposition history can prove that every failure remains blocking until supported by the required evidence.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The approved gate policy defines the evidence and approver fields required to dismiss each test-failure class.
Every dismissed test failure has a complete authenticated evidence record satisfying its bound gate policy.

controls.statement: Contract tests cover internal and external interfaces.
controls.primary_reason: A complete approved interface inventory can be compared exactly with current contract-test identities and results for each internal and external interface.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The approved release scope provides a complete stable inventory of internal and external interfaces requiring contract tests.
Every inventoried interface has a current successful contract-test result bound to the assessed producer and consumer versions.

controls.statement: Compatibility tests cover supported clients and versions.
controls.primary_reason: The approved support matrix is a finite policy input, allowing exact comparison with current compatibility-test coverage and outcomes.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The approved support record lists every supported client and version combination for the release.
Every supported client-version combination has a current compatibility-test result against the assessed release.

controls.statement: Migration, upgrade, mixed-version, downgrade, rollback, and roll-forward scenarios are tested.
controls.primary_reason: An approved release-transition matrix defines applicable scenarios, and each finite scenario can be matched with current execution evidence.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The versioned transition policy identifies which migration, upgrade, mixed-version, downgrade, rollback, and roll-forward scenarios apply.
Every applicable transition scenario has a current execution result bound to the exact source and target versions.

controls.statement: Performance tests cover load, stress, spike, endurance, and capacity limits.
controls.primary_reason: Approved workload profiles and capacity limits provide fixed inputs, so required load, stress, spike, endurance, and capacity executions can be verified.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The approved performance plan defines numeric profiles, durations, limits, and expected outcomes for all five required test classes.
Every approved performance case has a current execution result bound to the assessed artifact and production-like environment.

controls.statement: Accessibility testing combines automation with manual keyboard and assistive-technology checks.
controls.primary_reason: The statement requires the presence of three test modes, which can be established by authenticated automated, manual-keyboard, and assistive-technology execution records.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: A current automated accessibility scan result is bound to the assessed interface snapshot and tool version.
Current manual keyboard and assistive-technology test records identify tester, journey, environment, combination, and result.

controls.statement: Tests verify the actual artifact intended for production.
controls.primary_reason: The test evidence artifact digest can be compared directly with the immutable digest of the artifact named in the production release record.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every required test result identifies an artifact digest exactly equal to the intended production artifact digest.

controls.statement: Evidence identifies test version, data, environment, build, and result.
controls.primary_reason: Test version, data, environment, build, and result are explicit typed evidence fields whose presence and identity bindings are objectively validatable.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every test-evidence record contains test version, data-set identity, environment identity, build or artifact digest, and structured outcome.

controls.statement: Failed tests are linked to fixes and successful retests.
controls.primary_reason: Stable failure identities and authenticated change and retest records permit exact linkage from each failure through a fix to a later successful retest.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every failed required test has a linked change record identifying the attempted fix and affected source or artifact identity.
Each linked fix has a later successful retest of the same test identity against the resulting artifact.

controls.statement: A supported browser and device matrix is documented.
controls.primary_reason: The requirement is documentation of an intended support policy, so explicit browser, version, device, and viewport entries are fixed record facts.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The authenticated support record contains a versioned browser and device matrix with explicit versions, form factors, and policy status.

controls.statement: Client and server validation produce consistent outcomes.
controls.primary_reason: A finite approved validation-case inventory allows the same inputs to be submitted to client and server validators and their normalized outcomes compared exactly.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The approved validation contract enumerates input cases and normalized expected outcome fields for every client-server validated operation.
Client and server validators return equal normalized outcomes for every inventoried case.

controls.statement: The required WCAG version and conformance level are documented.
controls.primary_reason: The required WCAG edition and conformance level are explicit versioned policy fields whose presence and recognized values are objectively validatable.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The authenticated accessibility policy records one recognized WCAG version and required conformance level for the assessed product scope.

controls.statement: Automated accessibility scans pass within the accepted threshold.
controls.primary_reason: The control explicitly uses an accepted threshold, so pinned automated scan results can be compared exactly to its versioned numeric failure policy.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The approved accessibility policy binds a scanner identity and version, scan scope, accepted severity or count threshold, and evidence freshness.
A current automated accessibility scan covers the bound scope and its normalized findings satisfy every accepted threshold.

controls.statement: An accessibility statement and issue-reporting path exist.
controls.primary_reason: The exact requirement is existence of two public resources, which can be discovered and schema-checked without deciding full accessibility conformance.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: A current accessibility statement exists at an approved public location and identifies the assessed product or service.
A working public accessibility issue-reporting path is linked from the statement and accepts a bounded non-submitting reachability check.

controls.statement: Accessibility remains part of regression testing after launch.
controls.primary_reason: Current CI policy and test history can prove that the approved accessibility regression suite remains configured and executes after launch changes.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The approved post-launch regression profile identifies the required accessibility test suite and applicable change triggers.
Current CI configuration runs the bound accessibility suite for every applicable trigger and retains its latest result.
